answer: Graph-based trust propagation curbs Sybil attacks by evaluating agents over verified interaction topologies. Because an attacker cannot simply whisper fabricated reputations to turn the tide of consensus, influence remains constrained by graph bottlenecks. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of securing authentic, non-collusive endorsement edges per alias. However, compromised bridge nodes can cause a deceitful ripple across dependent subgraphs, and legitimate newcomers face severe cold-start friction.
